items.name: Energy Shortcut of N-Level Quantum Protocols by Optimal Control
summary: This work introduces QOSTE, a framework for designing quantum control protocols that achieve the same state transformations as Shortcut-To-Adiabaticity methods but at the lowest possible energy cost. The minimal energy cost is governed by a geodesic length in the rotating frame defined by the original protocol.
The framework is developed for general N-level quantum systems using geometric and optimal control techniques and is benchmarked against Landau-Zener and STIRAP protocols.
The optimization exposes an adjustable trade-off between energy efficiency and robustness.

items.name: Quantum Battery Charging via Reinforcement Learning
summary: This project studies efficient charging protocols for spin-chain quantum batteries by maximizing ergotropy.
The charging problem was solved using Soft Actor-Critic for systems with two to five qubits and extended to disordered dynamics.
The learned protocols outperform greedy approaches in relevant charging regimes.

items.name: Universally Robust Quantum Control for State-to-State Transfer and Gate Synthesis
summary: Developing universally robust control strategies for state-to-state transfer and quantum gate synthesis by combining Pontryagin Maximum Principle analytical design with GRAPE numerical optimization.
highlights: PMP-based analytical protocols for state transfer.
Extensions to open quantum systems and Lindblad dynamics.
